entries.answer:
“Unconditionally” is about loving someone without making that love dependent on them being perfect, polished, or easy to love. The speaker says she sees the other person’s insecurities and “dirty laundry,” yet chooses acceptance rather than judgment.

## What the lyrics mean

- “Did I get too close?” reflects the fear of being truly known—of someone seeing the hidden, awkward, flawed parts of you.
- “All your insecurities / all the dirty laundry / never made me blink” means: *your past, imperfections, and vulnerability do not make me withdraw.*
- “Come just as you are” and “don’t need apologies” offer emotional safety. The person does not have to perform perfection to deserve affection.
- “I’ll take your bad days with your good / walk through the storm” expresses commitment during difficult periods, not only when life or the relationship feels easy.
- The bridge—“Acceptance is the key … Will you do the same for me?”—adds an important reciprocal side: she wants to be accepted with the same openness she is offering.

## Not only romantic love

Although it can be heard as a romantic ballad, Katy Perry described it as a broader, “transcendent” kind of love: it can apply to partners, close friends, or a parent’s love for a child. She connected its inspiration to seeing what she regarded as pure affection among children during a UNICEF visit to Madagascar.[1][2]

In short, the song says: **You can let your guard down with me; I will love the real you, including the parts you fear will make you unlovable.**
